sections.label: Town Councils residents and monies
sections.summary: Town Councils serve over 3.2 million residents and manage over $1.6 billion, up from 2.4 million residents and $300 million in the early 1990s.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Today, Town Councils serve more than 3.2 million residents and collectively manage over $1.6 billion worth of public and residents' monies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This is a significant increase from 2.4 million residents and $300 million in the early 1990s.

sections.label: MND powers and 2015 Motion
sections.summary: MND may step in only as a last resort, and Parliament unanimously passed a February 2015 Motion calling for strengthening the Town Councils legislative framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: MND has powers to step in, only as a last resort, and in very limited circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And this is why Parliament unanimously passed a Motion in February 2015 that called for, among other things, I quote, "strengthening of the legislative framework for Town Councils".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Town Councils Act seek to address the limitations of the current legislative framework, while adhering to the original spirit and intent of the Act.

sections.label: Clause 12 commercial activities
sections.summary: Clause 12 clarifies that Town Councils are not to carry out commercial activities inconsistent with their core functions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 12 clarifies that Town Councils are not to carry out commercial activities that are inconsistent with their core functions.

sections.label: Offence of unlawful charges
sections.summary: It will now be an offence for a Town Council to impose unlawful charges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In addition, it will now be an offence for a Town Council to impose unlawful charges.

sections.label: Clause 14 agency cooperation
sections.summary: Clause 14 requires Town Councils to cooperate with agencies and public officers and grant access to and use of common property, such as for NEA CCTV cameras.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 14 requires Town Councils to cooperate with these agencies and public officers and grant them access to and use of common property, for instance, allowing the National Environment Agency (NEA) to install closed circuit television (CCTV) cameras to catch or deter high-rise littering.

sections.label: Clause 14 emergency preparations
sections.summary: Clause 14 allows MND to direct Town Councils to make emergency-related preparations, for instance ensuring essential services remain available.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 14 allows MND to direct Town Councils to make emergency-related preparations, for instance, to ensure that essential services remain available.

sections.label: Audited statements submission deadline
sections.summary: Clause 21 sets a six-month timeframe from financial year-end for Town Councils to submit audited statements to MND for Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To strengthen public and regulatory oversight of Town Councils' finances, clause 21 now specifies a timeframe of six months from the financial year (FY)-end for Town Councils to submit their audited statements to MND for presentation to Parliament.

sections.label: Lift Replacement Fund requirement
sections.summary: The Bill requires Town Councils to establish a ring-fenced Lift Replacement Fund, with clause 18 ensuring sufficient funds are set aside.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, the Bill will require Town Councils to establish a Lift Replacement Fund (LRF) that is ring-fenced for lift-related replacement and upgrading works.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 18 ensures that Town Councils set aside sufficient funds in the LRF, as lift expenditures are large and backloaded.

sections.label: MND investigative and enforcement powers
sections.summary: Clause 24 introduces a new Part VI A allowing MND to take investigative and enforcement actions on regulatory breaches or systemic weaknesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As regulator, MND must also have powers to conduct regular health checks for Town Councils, look into suspected irregularities and, where necessary, take prompt and effective actions to safeguard residents' interests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 24 of the Bill thus introduces a new Part VI A that allows MND to take the necessary investigative and enforcement actions to address potential regulatory breaches or systemic weaknesses in the Town Councils in a timely and calibrated manner.

sections.label: Investigations and rectification orders
sections.summary: MND may direct an investigation into suspected material irregularities and issue a rectification order for deficiencies or irregularities found.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Second, if there are reasonable grounds to suspect a material irregularity in a Town Council's affairs, MND may direct an investigation to be undertaken to establish if there was a contravention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, where the compliance reviews or investigations throw up deficiencies in the running of a Town Council or irregularities in its financial affairs, MND may follow up by issuing a rectification order.

sections.label: New penalty provisions
sections.summary: The Bill introduces new penalty provisions, in addition to the three in the Town Councils Act, in three key areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In addition to the three penalty provisions in the Town Councils Act, the Bill will introduce new penalty provisions to hold Town Councils accountable in three key areas.

sections.label: Improved Town Council governance
sections.summary: The proposed amendments to the Town Councils Act will further improve corporate governance, transparency and public accountability of Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the Town Councils Act will further improve corporate governance, transparency and public accountability of the Town Councils.

sections.label: Town Council audited accounts requirement
sections.summary: The passage supports requiring Town Councils to submit audited accounts within six months and display them online within 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I also agree to the implementation of the new requirement as stipulated in section 38.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This requires all Town Councils to submit their audited accounts and financial statement within six months after the close of the FY to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In particular, I believe the new requirement under section 38 (13A) will further strengthen corporate governance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This amendment to the Act will require Town Councils to display their audited accounts, financial statements and the auditor's report at an online location accessible to all residents within 30 days after it has presented the report to Parliament.

sections.label: HDB defects liability period management
sections.summary: The passage proposes HDB manage new flats and common property during the defects liability period, as private developers do.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This includes ensuring that all defects identified during the defects liability period are properly rectified before it is handed over to the Town Council for management.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Thus, I would propose that HDB adopt the practice by private developers, where they will be required to take charge of the management of new flats and common property during the defects liability period.

sections.label: WP concerns over Part VI A
sections.summary: The Workers' Party does not oppose raising governance standards but has concerns over Part VI A's oversight powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party (WP) does not oppose raising governance standards for Town Councils, but we have specific concerns over the new Part VI A of the Bill which gives intrusive oversight powers to MND directed by political officeholders of any incumbent government, not just the PAP.

sections.label: WP position on six amendments
sections.summary: WP does not oppose five of six amendments but says government oversight mechanisms over Town Councils could be abused.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, WP does not oppose five of the six amendments proposed in the Explanatory Statement to the Bill, namely, to promote and strengthen effective and efficient governance and accountability of Town Councils; to foster a culture of personal integrity and accountability for administrative officials of the Town Council; to ensure sound financial management; to promote better governance and to clarify the role of Town Councils in emergency planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the introduction of oversight mechanisms and monitoring powers over the Town Councils that are in the hands of the Government has the potential for abuse.

sections.label: HDB intervention and MP autonomy
sections.summary: The passage says HDB should intervene only for public health, safety and order, and clause 24 diminishes MPs' political autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, as such, to preserve the political autonomy of the MPs and self-reliance of the people, HDB should only intervene when there are hazards to public health, public safety and public order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In principle, clause 24 of the Bill is problematic on these three points by reversing and diminishing the political autonomy of the elected MPs in relation to MND, which overseas HDB.

sections.label: Risks of MND oversight powers
sections.summary: The passage states the oversight risks politicising the Public Service and subordinating elected MPs to unelected bureaucracy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, it risks politicisation of the Public Service where MND risks becoming a tool of the ruling party of the day to fix the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, it causes the elected MPs to answer to the unelected bureaucracy, subordinating the elected mandate of MPs to the Executive branch.

sections.label: Resident interest and HDB poll
sections.summary: A 2009 Straits Times report said residents did not seem more interested in their estates, and a 2013 poll found close to 80% wanted HDB to replace Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mdm Speaker, as late as 2009, a Straits Times report quoting the then Senior Minister Goh Chok Tong noted that in spite of the Town Councils' existence, residents did not seem to take a greater interest in the estates they lived in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was noteworthy that one public poll commissioned by the Straits Times in 2013 found that close to 80% of those polled wish to have HDB replace Town Councils in the provision of services to residents.

sections.label: 2013 poll and MP value
sections.summary: The 2013 poll polled 50 people and 41 wanted estate management returned to HDB, but the speaker said there is value in having MPs run Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The 2013 poll polled 50 people and 41 of them wanted estate management returned to HDB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But to clarify, as I mentioned in my speech, there is value in having MPs run Town Councils.

sections.label: Inspectors entering Town Councils
sections.summary: On inspectors who could enter a Town Council under clause 24, the speaker suggested the existing Town Councils Act provision for an independent agent is potentially sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Senior Minister of State's first question was with regard to the inspectors who, under clause 24, could come into a Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I would suggest that the provision that the Town Councils Act currently provides for, which is, for an independent agent to potentially look into issues which MND feels the Town Council ought to, is potentially sufficient.

sections.label: Part VI A independent auditors
sections.summary: The speaker asked whether explaining that Part VI A lets MND appoint independent auditors who report to MND and the Town Council would change the other side's position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If I were to explain to him that Part VI A allows for MND to appoint independent auditors who would then conduct compliance reviews or investigations and who are then required by the legislation to report to both MND and the Town Council, would that change his and his Party's position?

sections.label: Six-month submission deadline
sections.summary: The new section 38(11) amendment requires a Town Council to submit documents within six months after the financial year closes, and the speaker cited PRPGTC's 8.5 months and AHTC's 15 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The new amendment under section 38(11) requires a Town Council to submit these documents within six months after the close of the FY.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Pasir Ris-Punggol Town Council (PRPGTC) took 8.5 months to submit our audited financial statements on the distribution of assets and liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On the other hand, in 2015, after the General Election when Punggol East returned to PRPGTC, AHTC took 15 months in total.

sections.label: PRPGTC qualified financial statements
sections.summary: PRPGTC's FY2015/2016 audited financial statements were qualified because the audit of Punggol East SMC's financial statements as at 30 November had not been completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: PRPGTC's FY2015/2016 audited financial statements were then qualified on the basis that the audit of the financial statements of Punggol East SMC as at 30 November has not been completed.

sections.label: Criminal liability for Town Council officers
sections.summary: Clause 25 creates a new section 48A making Town Council Chairman, Secretary or purported officers criminally liable for certain Town Council offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Clause 25 introduces a new section 48A that imposes on the Chairman or Secretary of a Town Council, or any person who was purporting to act in any such capacity, criminal liability for certain offences committed by the Town Council in certain circumstances.

sections.label: Prof Boo on S$23 million payments
sections.summary: Prof El'fred Boo said a major finding centred on payments of at least S$23 million that could suggest the agent approving and paying itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Prof El'fred Boo further added, I quote, "One of the major findings centred on a series of payments of at least S$23 million, which, in the absence of approved controls in a severely weak control environment amid a conflict-of-interest situation, could suggest that the agent is approving and making payments to itself.

sections.label: Town Council Amendment Bill accountability
sections.summary: The amendments ensure better public accountability and strengthen financial management, with MND oversight catching problems early before funds are mismanaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Mdm Speaker, the amendments in the Town Council (Amendment) Bill will ensure better public accountability and strengthen financial management in the Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As Town Councils manage a substantial amount of public funds, the proposed regulatory oversight by MND will ensure that problems that are identified early can be nipped in the bud before they become a liability to all the residents if funds are mismanaged.

sections.label: Data format and late sinking fund transfers
sections.summary: Data came in unusable PDF format and information was late, affecting service to residents; AHTC's sinking fund transfers were late even before withheld Government transfers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: For example, data were provided in the PDF format instead in the format that we could actually use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: We were also not given the information that we required in a timely manner and these all affected our ability to be able to serve our residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: I just said that if a Town Council is late in the transfer of sinking funds, it could imply the two things which I have mentioned in the speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: And I would like to state, looking at the records of AHTC, the transfer of sinking funds was late even before Government transfers were being withheld.

sections.label: First $10 million transfer timing
sections.summary: They explained they made the first transfer of $10 million within three months of the handover.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: On the second point with regard to the transfer, we did explain, we did make the first transfer of $10 million within three months of the handover.

sections.label: Influence over MA holding positions
sections.summary: Clause 13 introduces section 20(1A) barring anyone with significant influence over the MA from holding Town Council Secretary, General Manager, Finance Manager or deputy positions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Clause 13 introduces a new section 20(1A) that a person who exercises a significant influence over the MA cannot hold a Town Council position of Secretary, General Manager, Finance Manager or their deputies.

sections.label: Town Council Secretaries and GMs
sections.summary: The passage asks how many current Town Council Secretaries and GMs will have to leave their posts when the provision takes effect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Can the Minister tell the House how many of the current slate of Town Council Secretaries and GMs will have to leave their posts when this provision is effective?

sections.label: New Part VIA Minister powers
sections.summary: Part VIA introduces sections 43A to 43H giving the Minister power over compliance reviews and investigations into Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Part VIA introduces new sections 43A to 43H, basically giving tremendous power to the Minister to devise strategies for compliance reviews on Town Councils and for the Minister to order investigations into particular Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: This Bill presents an about-turn from the original intent of Town Councils, which was to empower MPs to run towns with minimal interference from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: These new provisions are also a likely response to the Court judgment in the case filed by the Ministry against AHPETC, where it was held by both the High Court and the Court of Appeal that the Ministry was not the proper party to sue Town Councils.

sections.label: Reviving AGO Town Council audits
sections.summary: The passage proposes reviving AGO audits of Town Councils, with a few picked each year for audit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In our view, instead of having the Minister direct partisan investigations, we should revive the audits by AGO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Town Councils were in the past audited by AGO and we believe that AGO should be tasked to audit Town Councils on a rational basis, that is, a few Town Councils should be picked each year for audit.

sections.label: Independent housing tribunal proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes an independent housing tribunal to mediate and adjudicate disputes over public housing management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: It is necessary to put in place a simple mechanism to help resolve issues that crop up from time to time between MND, HDB, NEA and other agencies and Town Councils and residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: We suggest the setting up of an independent housing tribunal that tries to mediate and adjudicate disputes relating to the management of public housing.

sections.label: WP position on the Bill
sections.summary: The passage states tribunal decisions are binding unless appealable on error of law, and WP will oppose the Bill if clause 24 is not removed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Where the tribunal makes a decision, its decisions will be binding, unless on an error of law, which would be appealable to the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: For the reasons I have stated, the Bill has some merits, such as explicitly requiring management of conflicts of interest and accountability which we fully support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But there are other parts, such as the new Part VIA which are fundamentally flawed to the extreme conflicts of interest they perpetuate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The provisions are also prone to abuse by the incumbent Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: We ask the Government to remove clause 24 that introduces the new Part VIA and instead use the existing laws and rotational audits by AGO to safeguard the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In addition, we ask the Government to set up a housing tribunal along the lines of independence suggested.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: If the Government cannot agree to remove clause 24, WP will oppose the Bill.

sections.label: Town Council annual budgets
sections.summary: The passage states most Town Councils have annual budgets ranging between $30 million and $40 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The annual budget of most Town Councils range between $30 million and $40 million.

sections.label: Tender bids for repairs
sections.summary: A recent tender for repairs and redecoration of 15 blocks of flats and a hawker centre drew bids all above $1.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Just to give the House a flavour of the amount involved, in a recent tender to carry out repairs and redecoration of 15 blocks of flats and a hawker centre, the tender bids alone were all above $1.6 million.

sections.label: Audited financial statements deadline
sections.summary: Clause 21 requires the Town Council to submit audited financial statements to the Minister within six months after the close of the financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Clause 21 of the Bill requires the Town Council to submit its audited financial statements to the Minister within six months after the close of FY.

sections.label: Audited accounts and HDB cooperation
sections.summary: Clause 14 introduces section 21A obliging the Town Council to work with HDB and listed statutory bodies, alongside submitting audited accounts for accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Submission of audited financial accounts to the Government is important because if there are any issues with the accounts, it is important that all parties sit down quickly to find out what these issues are and how to resolve them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It is also a form of public accountability because the Government gives each Town Council grants worth millions of dollars every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Clause 14 of the Bill introduces a new section 21A which imposes on the Town Council an obligation to work with HDB and any statutory body performing the functions listed at section 21A(1)(b) of the Bill.

sections.label: Lift replacement fund requirement
sections.summary: Clause 18 introduces a new requirement for the Town Council to establish a lift replacement fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next point is clause 18 which talks about the lift replacement fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This clause introduces a new requirement for the Town Council to establish a lift replacement fund.

sections.label: Personal liability for Chairman, Secretary
sections.summary: The clause inserts a new section 48A into the Town Councils Act, introducing personal liability for the Chairman or Secretary of the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The clause inserts a new section 48A to the Town Councils Act and introduced the concept of personal liability for the Chairman or Secretary of the Town Council.

sections.label: Support for clause 24 Part VIA
sections.summary: The speaker supports clause 24 Part VIA, saying it gives better public accountability and stronger financial management if a Town Council is badly managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, if WP is able to manage the Town Council well and with proper governance, then clause 24 or Part VIA will not be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If my Town Council is badly managed, then I will expect that the Government will look after the interest of the residents and would interfere and would ensure that the compliance of the Town Council is taken seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: As an example, if Mr Pritam Singh's Town Council chooses not to transfer monies into its sinking fund, or uses its revenues for its routine operational expenses only, should the Government not be concerned that his Town Council is unable to carry out its functions, to carry out cyclical works in the future?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Should the Government then do nothing to protect the interests of its citizens?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, for that reason, Mdm Speaker, I do support clause 24 Part VI A of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, I have no doubt that it is the right and responsible thing to do, as it would result in better public accountability and strengthen financial management.

sections.label: Town Council financial accounting problem
sections.summary: WP managed the Town Council for 20 years without major problems, but the problem is financial accounting, attributed to AIM, with a new tender expected to improve things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: Yes, WP has been managing the Town Council in the past 20 years without major problems or hiccups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: What the problem is, is financial accounting problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: But I would like to say and reiterate again − I would say that the problem is thanks to the company called Action Information Management Pte Ltd (AIM).

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Low Thia Khiang, you should confine your clarification to what Mr Lim Biow Chuan said.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: I wish to inform the House that we have a new tender for a new financial accounting system and we expect things to be improved.

sections.label: Expanded conflict of interest provisions
sections.summary: Clause 9 requires Town Council members' conflicts to be placed on record and suspends powers of staff in conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: The expanded conflict of interest provisions in clause 9 of the amendment Bill, therefore, seeks to achieve this by requiring conflicts which members of Town Council may have in relation to a particular issue to be placed on record and by requiring a suspension of the exercise of powers of staff of a Town Council who may be in a position of conflict.

sections.label: Public notification of conflicts
sections.summary: Conflicts raised should be publicly notified to residents, and HDB approval required for Town Council fund expenditure despite conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Given that such conflicts of interest may be connected to the spending of public money, I believe that it would be in the interest of Singaporeans if, first, any such conflict that has been raised are publicly notified to residents of the town and, secondly, if the matter involves the expenditure of Town Council funds, for the approval of HDB to be required to proceed with the matter notwithstanding the conflict.

sections.label: Personal liability for breach
sections.summary: Proposed section 48A makes the Chairman or Secretary personally liable for a Town Council's breach of section 21A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: The proposed new section 48A gives further bite to the proposed section 21A by stipulating that the Chairman or Secretary of the Town Council may be personally liable for a Town Council's breach of section 21A.

sections.label: Amended Town Councils Act duties
sections.summary: The amended Act requires Town Councils to ensure timely collection of money payable and proper spending of money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: The amended Town Councils Act will require Town Councils to, amongst other things, ensure timely collection of money payable and ensure money is properly spent by Town Councils.

sections.label: Incompetent governance and frustrated investigations
sections.summary: The amendment Bill addresses incompetent governance of Town Councils and attempts to frustrate investigations, including conduct in the Punggol East SMC handover.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: One, incompetent governance of Town Councils and, two, attempts to frustrate investigations by the Government into the affairs of the Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: It is true that the amendment Bill does address conduct which WP engaged in in respect of the handover of funds attributable to Punggol East SMC.

sections.label: MND action against AHTC
sections.summary: MND took firm action against AHTC because AHTC did not meet standards required to protect the public interest in running its town.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: MND has taken firm action in respect of AHTC only because AHTC has not met the standards required to protect the public interest in its running of its town.

sections.label: Concerns raised about AHTC
sections.summary: Neutral parties including KPMG, the Courts and the Accountant-General's Office raised concerns about AHTC's affairs, and its auditors could not issue unqualified accounts in five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: In addition, it is not only MND which has raised concerns about the goings-on in AHTC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: It is well documented that neutral parties − KPMG, the Courts, the Accountant-General's Office − have all raised concerns about the affairs at AHTC, in particular, AHTC's own auditors have not been able to issue a set of unqualified accounts in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Among other things, KPMG referred to pervasive control failures, inadequate qualified personnel and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: I believe AHTC has only resolved less than half of the audit points which it is meant to address.

sections.label: AHTC sinking funds and accounts
sections.summary: AHTC had not returned $20 million of sinking funds, later returned it, and its final accounts showed it owed more than $4 million, which it paid after a letter of demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: On the first issue, at that time, after the elections, AHTC had yet to return the $20 million of sinking funds that we have transferred to AHTC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: That amount has been returned but the final accounts which they had sent to us, we received only on 24 February.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: And it showed, by their calculation, that they still owed us more than $4 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: They have paid that back after we served a letter of demand on them.

sections.label: AHTC second and third accounts
sections.summary: The second set of accounts was sent recently and voluntarily withdrawn, and a third set followed on 24 February 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: The second set of accounts were sent recently, and they also voluntarily withdrew it for whatever reason, because they did not have enough time to examine it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: And then they followed up with a third set of accounts on 24 February 2017.

sections.label: Clarifying substantial trading activities
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify what is meant by substantial trading or financial activities and whether clearer guidelines will be published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Having said that, can the Minister clarify what exactly is meant by "substantial trading or financial activities?" Will the Ministry be publishing clearer guidelines with regard to this?

sections.label: Guarantees for Town Councils
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify whether guarantees exist for Town Councils to raise concerns about directions from Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this regard, can the Minister clarify if there are such guarantees in place for Town Councils to raise their concerns about directions from Statutory Boards?

sections.label: By-laws inconsistency and appeal process
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will determine if by-laws are inconsistent, who decides, whether there is an appeal, and whether a draft will be released to Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry determine if the by-laws are "inconsistent?" Who will determine this and is there an appeal process?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide more clarifications about the model by-laws and whether a draft will be released to the Town Councils for our input and feedback soon?

sections.label: Town Council and MP role
sections.summary: The passage states the Town Council is the key instrument for an elected MP to influence constituents' living environment and that its municipal role should not change.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Town Council, as we all know, is the key instrument through which the elected MP for that constituency is able to directly influence the living environment of his constituents, and the performance and integrity of the Town Council serves as a bellwether of the Member's fidelity to his or her residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I feel that this municipal role of a sitting Member should not change, as the separation of the municipal and legislative roles will dilute the relationship between an MP and his constituents or could even result in unproductive conflicts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, it has to be acknowledged, as many Members have done, that the Town Council is primarily a custodian of the properties within the Town, but also has heavy responsibilities regarding the immediate day-to-day upkeep of the precincts and also the long-term maintenance and rejuvenation of the Town, a key case in point being the need to plan for the replacement of lifts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Unlike the management of private housing projects, the Town Council has to factor in future large infrastructure investments into their operational considerations.

sections.label: Town Council financial discipline amendments
sections.summary: The passage states amendments require audited financial reports within six months, a conflicts registry, fines up to $5,000, and prosecution of key decision-makers.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendments will help tighten financial discipline and strengthen accountability and transparency by requiring Town Councils to submit the audited financial reports within six months of the FY and keep a registry of disclosures on conflicts of interest involving staff members or employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is important as residents do pay conservancy charges and it is important that they know where the money goes to.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It further stresses that Town Councils that fail to comply with the Act will be fined up to $5,000 and key decision-makers can be prosecuted for the failure.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In view of the fact that Town Councils in the first place were created to decentralise the estate management of the residential town, therefore, do the amendments intend to include a provision to allow different Town Council management regimes in the future?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If, or should the Town Council fail or does not perform satisfactorily or perform up to par, how would the Ministry, as the body with regulatory and oversight over the Town Council, deal with it?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Clause 18 of the Town Council (Amendment) Bill seeks to amend section 33 to establish a new sinking fund called LRF.

sections.label: MND co-funding LRF
sections.summary: The passage states MND is co-funding LRF by matching 50% of the Town Council's contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, I am glad that MND is co-funding LRF, matching 50% of the Town Council's contributions to LRF.

sections.label: MND lift grant
sections.summary: The passage states MND will provide a grant of $600 per lift owned and maintained by Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, I am also glad that MND will be providing a grant of $600 per lift owned and maintained by the Town Councils.

sections.label: Punishment under clause 48A(1)
sections.summary: The passage states the highest punishment under clause 48A(1) is one year's imprisonment, or a $5,000 fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The highest punishment under clause 48A(1) is one year's imprisonment, or a fine of $5,000, or both.

sections.label: Town Council fine for contravention
sections.summary: The Town Council can impose a fine if a resident contravenes this rule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If the resident contravenes this rule, the Town Council can impose a fine.

sections.label: Town Council messy accounts
sections.summary: A certain Town Council's accounts are so messy its own independent auditor dare not approve them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Like in a certain Town Council, its accounts are so messy that even their own independent auditor dare not approve the accounts.

sections.label: Amendment strengthens Town Council transparency
sections.summary: The amendment aims to strengthen transparency and control of Town Councils to prevent similar mishaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If a listed company cannot pass external auditing, the share price of the company will drop significantly and the shareholders will lose confidence in the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, the particular Town Council that cannot even pass external auditing is still untouched even today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, the very purpose of this amendment is to strengthen the transparency and control of the Town Councils to prevent similar mishaps from happening.

sections.label: Clause 14 Town Council cooperation
sections.summary: Clause 14 requires Town Councils to work with HDB or statutory authorities or risk penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The first is the amendment suggested in clause 14 of the Bill where it was stated in absolute terms that Town Councils must work cooperatively and collaboratively with HDB or any statutory authority or public officer when they discharge their duties or risk being penalised for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the amendments of the Bill will vest HDB and any statutory authority with the power to enforce penalties on Town Councils if they are deemed to be non-compliant to the agency's request, I hope that this power will be exercised only when HDB and the other statutory authorities have exhausted all other means of bringing that particular Town Council in line with its mandated duty of serving the interests of the residents.

sections.label: Billing for car park bollards
sections.summary: The question asks which agency should be responsible for billing bollards where safety issues arose from HDB's car park design.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My question is: which agency should be responsible for the billing of the bollards, in this instance, where safety issues have risen from an inherent design flaw or a wrong decision of a car park that was designed and built by HDB?

sections.label: Lift maintenance costs and technicians
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for continued grants and asks if HDB and MND will seek foreign worker quota dispensation for lift technicians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The cost of lift maintenance is likely to increase exponentially over time, especially when ageing estates need to replace entire batches of lifts when the lifts reach the end of their service lifespan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I hope that the Government will continue to provide the grants to Town Councils to defray the servicing and replacement cost of lifts and also adjust the quantum of both grants from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Indeed, it was recently mentioned in a CNA report that Singapore would need an additional 1,000 lift technicians over the next three years in order to meet our overall lift maintenance needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The lack of skilled technicians in lift servicing is a worrying concern since the demands for these technicians will only increase over time and the biggest bugbear that prevents new entrants from entering the sector is the relative tough job that technicians need to do and the lack of career prospects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given that we need more than 1,000 technicians over the next three years and the relative difficulty in attracting Singaporeans and locals into the sector, would HDB and MND work with MOM to get special dispensation with regard to the foreign worker quota for this job category?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe the waiver of the foreign worker quota will, in the short and medium term, help alleviate the shortage of manpower in the sector while we attempt to build a stronger Singaporean Core in this area of work.

sections.label: Town Councils character unchanged
sections.summary: The proposed amendments do not fundamentally alter the character, roles and functions of Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The proposed amendments do not fundamentally alter the character of Town Councils or their roles and functions.

sections.label: Bill clarifies Town Council boundaries
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies existing boundaries for Town Councils, adds safeguards and compliance mechanisms, and requires publication of key appointments and financial statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Bill simply provides clarity on some of the existing boundaries within which Town Councils operate, for instance, Town Councils being subordinate to public laws and statutory authorities carrying out statutory duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Bill also puts in place safeguards and compliance mechanisms to enable MND as a regulator, as it has always been, to exercise more effective oversight of Town Councils on residents' behalf.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For example, the Bill requires Town Councils to publish their key appointments and financial statements.

sections.label: Minister recusal and officeholders
sections.summary: If the Minister recuses himself, other officeholders must exercise those powers, and if all are recused, another Minister is appointed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the case of the Town Councils Act, if the Minister is required to recuse himself, then the other officeholders will have to step up and exercise those powers with the same good faith and with the same obligations as the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And if all the officials or the MND political officeholders have to be recused, then some other Minister will have to be appointed to exercise those powers.

sections.label: MND appoints independent inspectors
sections.summary: Under the Bill, MND can appoint an independent auditor or independent panel as inspectors for compliance reviews and investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, for the purposes of compliance reviews and investigations, under the Bill, MND can similarly appoint an independent auditor or independent panel as inspectors to carry out the review.

sections.label: MND rectification order scope
sections.summary: MND need not issue a rectification order, and any order only reflects what the Town Council ought to have done to comply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If so, MND will not need to step in to issue any rectification order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But in any event, MND's rectification order can only reflect what the Town Council ought to have done in the first place and will not require the Town Council to take any action over and above what is necessary to bring the Town Council into compliance with the Town Councils Act and its subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: HDB 2015 Court intervention
sections.summary: Court transcripts recorded HDB seeking the Court's intervention in 2015 to appoint an independent auditor to look into AHTC's problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But to really know what it is, let us look at what was said in Court, recorded by Court transcripts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This was when HDB sought the Court's intervention in 2015 to appoint an independent auditor to look into AHTC's problems and to take necessary action.

sections.label: MND reviews Town Council accounts
sections.summary: MND receives Town Councils' financial statements yearly and gives them a chance to correct inconsistencies and accounting errors, as it did for AHTC's FY2015/2016 accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is what our public servants do and what this team of officers and their predecessors have been doing for the past 28 years of the Town Councils' existence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But each year, MND receives the Town Councils' submitted financial statements and gives them the opportunity to correct inconsistencies and accounting errors in their accounts, part of due diligence that MND public servants undertake for every Town Council as they are submitted to this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, this is exactly what MND Secretariat did, I am told, for AHTC's FY2015/2016 accounts yesterday.

sections.label: Fines on key decision-makers
sections.summary: A fine imposed on a key decision-maker must be borne by the individual found liable and not paid from Town Council funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is for individual Town Councils to decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I will clarify, though, that a fine imposed on a key decision-maker, or a person purporting to act in that capacity, it is to be borne by the individual who is found liable for the offence and not be paid from the Town Council's funds.

sections.label: Town Council investment safeguards
sections.summary: Town Councils may invest funds to counter inflation subject to financial rules, and a new provision prevents risky ventures like running subsidiary companies or unlicensed activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Town Councils may also invest their funds to counter inflation, subject to safeguards in the Town Councils' financial rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, to Mr Louis Ng's question on what "substantial trading" means, the new provision prevents Town Councils from undertaking risky ventures, by deviating from the key mandate, for example, using Town Council funds to set up and run subsidiary companies or carrying out activities under the aegis of the Town Council which are unlicensed and incurring fines on the Town Councils' purse as a consequence.

sections.label: Town Councils blocking agency works
sections.summary: Examples given include a Town Council refusing to apply for EMA licences for HDB lift upgrading and one refusing NEA surveillance cameras for high-rise littering in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One example is where HDB's lift upgrading works were once held up by a Town Council which refused to apply for the relevant licences required from the Energy Market Agency (EMA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For example, one Town Council refused to allow NEA to deploy surveillance cameras to catch high-rise littering in 2014.

sections.label: MND arbitration and compliance orders
sections.summary: MND public officers will arbitrate if needed, and under the Bill a compliance order will be issued when agencies see it necessary to act on common property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And if MND needs to come in to try and arbitrate the matter, our public officers will do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I will assure Ms Sylvia Lim that under the Bill, if a compliance order has to be issued, it will be because the agencies see that it is necessary to carry on to do what it needs to do on common property.

sections.label: Additional Town Council by-laws
sections.summary: Town Councils can still introduce additional by-laws based on their needs as long as they are not inconsistent with the model by-laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Town Councils can still introduce additional by-laws based on their needs as long as they are not inconsistent with the model by-laws.

sections.label: Town Council insolvency early warning
sections.summary: Early warning signals let at-risk Town Councils act on cash flow, and MND can prescribe steps by rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This puts in place early warning signals, so that a Town Council, at risk of insolvency sometime down the road, can take timely steps to improve its cash flow situation and financial health, rather than wait for the situation to become dire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But if it comes to that, MND will now have powers to make rules that prescribe steps that the Town Council should take or should not take.

sections.label: Post-election Town Council handovers
sections.summary: The Bill lets MND make subsidiary legislation for post-election handovers between Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Bill allows MND to make subsidiary legislation in relation to post-election handovers between Town Councils.

sections.label: Minister can require handover information
sections.summary: In an impasse, the Minister can require an outgoing Town Council to give the taking-over Town Council information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the event of an impasse, the Minister can require an outgoing Town Council to furnish the necessary information to the taking-over Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The key, as I said earlier, is a willingness to work with each other, despite being of different partisan colours, to show maturity and to emphasise that the focus is, ultimately, on residents.

sections.label: HDB notifies Town Councils of completion
sections.summary: HDB notifies Town Councils three months before common property completion and meets on site one month before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, HDB will notify Town Councils of the completion of common property three months in advance, so as to allow Town Councils to plan their resources early and to arrange for subsequent meetings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It will also arrange for a meeting with the Town Council on site one month before completion so that the Town Council can take a look at the development and raise feedback early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This draft booklet was sent to all Town Councils on 1 March this year for comments.

sections.label: Lift replacement costs for Town Councils
sections.summary: Town Councils will need to replace about 24,000 lifts over 30 years at an estimated $6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To keep them reliable and safe, lifts need to be maintained regularly and replaced every 25 to 30 years, depending on specifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Based on our projections, over the next 30 years, Town Councils will need to progressively replace about 24,000 lifts across all HDB estates, at an estimated cost of about $6 billion.

sections.label: Minimum sinking fund contributions
sections.summary: Town Councils must set aside at least 14% of S&CC income and grants into LRF and 26% to the general sinking fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Town Councils will have to set aside a minimum of 14% of their S&CC income and Government grants into LRF and a minimum 26% to the general sinking fund.

sections.label: Extra funding for Town Councils
sections.summary: Extra funding for Town Councils adds up to over $100 million a year, doubling current annual funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As the chart on the screen shows, the extra funding that Town Councils will receive adds up to more than $100 million a year, or a billion dollars over the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is a substantial package, which is on top of the current S&CC Operating Grants that we issue to all Town Councils, and Goods and Services Tax (GST) Subvention Grants and the S&CC rebates, all of which amount to more than $120 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This effectively doubles the amount of annual funding that Town Councils currently receive.

sections.label: MND as Town Council regulator
sections.summary: The speaker says MND is the appropriate regulator and clause 43B would have an independent individual investigate all Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Yes, we have more powers today to intervene, but these powers are because the unspoken compact when the Town Councils were formed 28 years ago has been broken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That compact is premised on Town Councillors and elected Members, recognising the electoral accountability, the visibility to the residents, would do what is right to fix the problems and would proactively do it, as has been wont of many Town Councils by the Government who would report to CPIB and the Police when things are wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But in AHPETC's case, despite its external auditor's findings, despite the AGO's report, despite the findings by the High Court and Court of Appeal, and despite KPMG's report, take the view that, "Come, the reports do not say that definitively; yes, there is a cloud, but you prove it and I will sit tight." Even today, we have to wait for an independent panel, external from the Town Councillors, to take decisive action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, when it comes to whether MND is the appropriate regulator, I think it is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have indicated to Mr Pritam Singh that in regard to clause 43B, it would be an independent auditor, independent individual, who will conduct investigations of all Town Councils.

sections.label: AGO rotational audits of Town Councils
sections.summary: The proposal is that the AGO does rotational audits of all Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: To follow up on what the Senior Minister of State mentioned about the AGO, our proposal is that the AGO does rotational audits of all Town Councils.

sections.label: Health checks and investigations
sections.summary: The speaker describes health checks and compliance reviews, and investigations from reasonable suspicion of wrongdoing, and records WP dissent on Clause 24.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One is health checks, compliance reviews; and the other is where there are investigations arising from a reasonable suspicion of wrongdoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The AGO can already be triggered under the clauses in the Audit Act, as had been the case for AHPETC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Yes, Madam, we would like the WP Members' dissent to be specifically recorded that we cannot accept the Bill because of Clause 24.
